feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: NPR's expanded coverage of U.S. and world politics, the latest news from Congress and the White House and elections.

entry.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico reporters denied access to White House following Trump ban
entry.summary: Three reporters were blocked from the White House grounds Saturday morning, a day after President Trump said CNN, Politico, and MS NOW would be banned for reporting "FICTION and LIES."

entry.title: Week in Politics: Trump bans news outlets; Iran War; mail-in voting; interest rates
entry.summary: The Trump administration was frustrated both home and abroad this week.

entry.title: Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House
entry.summary: The president chalked the ban up to what he called unfavorable coverage, and he threatened that bans on other media companies could be coming.

entry.title: White House withdraws nomination of Lance Schroyer to lead ICE
entry.summary: President Trump's nominee to lead U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement was former Oklahoma state trooper Lance Schroyer. Three months after tapping him for the job, his name is being withdrawn.

entry.title: How Google is drafting AI chatbot laws around the country
entry.summary: As states push to regulate chatbots, tech companies are trying to write safety rules in ways that exempt some of their key products.

entry.title: Republican 'cavalry' arrives with a Trump-backed $150 million ad blitz in key races
entry.summary: To counter a difficult political environment, two Trump-aligned super PACs have reserved more than $150 million in ads — primarily in deep red House and Senate races that have now become competitive.

entry.title: A DHS email raises new questions about the Trump administration's election plans
entry.summary: A heavily redacted email from last year, reported first by NPR, reveals that DHS personnel shared a list of jurisdictions that offer election materials in non-English languages. It's unclear why.

entry.title: Some GOP candidates are still making election fraud claims. Voters want to move on
entry.summary: President Trump and some Republican battleground candidates are still embracing false claims about widespread election fraud in 2020, even as many GOP voters want them to move on.

entry.title: Republican candidate in Florida runs ads criticizing Trump's immigration enforcement
entry.summary: In a rare move, a House Republican running in a competitive race in South Florida is publicly breaking with President Trump. Maria Elvira Salazar represents a majority Hispanic district.

entry.title: Texas Republican candidate under fire for comment about university students of color
entry.summary: A Texas Republican's complaint that too many people of color were in a video of the crowd at a University of Texas football game set off condemnations.
